‘Ukrainians, Have You No Empathy?’: Russians Cry on Camera as Ukraine Strikes More Wildberries Warehouses — Russian sellers wept on camera and asked Ukrainians whether they had empathy after new drone strikes hit Wildberries logistics centers near St. Petersburg. Ukraine says the retailer’s warehouses support Russia’s military logistics by supplying drone components, navigation equipment, and other gear.

WATCH: Russia’s New Arena-M Anti-Drone System Fails in Action — Ukraine has shown footage of its drone ramming into the back of a Russian T-72B3A tank equipped with Moscow’s latest Arena-M anti-drone system, with previous criticism from Russian experts casting doubt on whether its radar can actually do what’s being advertised.

10 Killed, 100 Injured After Russian Missile Hits Defense Industry Event in Kyiv Region — A Russian ballistic missile strike on a training ground in the Kyiv region hosting a defense industry event killed 10 people and injured about 100. Prosecutors have launched parallel investigations into the attack and the organization of the event, while military experts questioned why it was held within range of Russian ballistic missiles.

Georgia Hit by Nationwide Blackout — Georgia was struck by a nationwide blackout around midnight on Friday, July 24, with authorities saying the exact cause remains unknown. At the time of writing, power is partially restored to parts of the country.

Russian Airstrike on Sloviansk Kills 5, Damages Latvian Consulate — Russian forces dropped two guided aerial bombs on Sloviansk, killing five people and injuring nine. The strike damaged homes, businesses, and the Honorary Consulate of Latvia, prompting Ukrainian prosecutors to open a war crimes investigation.

Romanian F-16 Downs Unidentified Drone During Russian Strike on Ukraine — Romanian President Nicușor Dan said his country’s F-16 downed an unidentified drone violating the airspace at around 11 a.m. on Friday, adding that an investigation is ongoing to establish the full circumstances.

Kyiv Hit by Rare Daytime Ballistic Missile Strike — Kyiv Post correspondents report multiple explosions in and around the city on Friday, July 24, as the Ukrainian Air Force warns of incoming ballistic missiles in a rare daytime attack. Currenly estimates suggest 12 missiles were launched, including ballistic missiles and the Tsirkon cruise missiles.

US Hits Russian Imports With New 12.5% Tariff — A new 12.5% US tariff on most Russian goods took effect on July 24 as part of a broader trade action against 60 economies over forced labor rules. The measure is separate from proposed secondary tariffs targeting countries that continue buying Russian energy.

Russian Bombs Destroy Nova Poshta Terminal in Izyum as 150,000 Lose Power in Chernihiv — Russia attacked Ukraine overnight with 5 missiles and 180 drones, destroying a Nova Poshta terminal in Izyum. Air defenses intercepted most targets, but strikes damaged infrastructure and left 150,000 people without electricity in Chernihiv.

'We Changed the Relationship': Zelensky Reveals What Happened in Private Trump Meeting — Zelensky said a private 20-minute meeting with Trump at the Vatican fundamentally changed their relationship after months of tensions. Media reports say the two leaders could meet again in Washington next week while Zelensky attends Sen. Lindsey Graham's funeral.

‘Significant Problems’ in Russian Banking System as Public Withdraws Cash en Masse — Russians have withdrawn more than 2.4 trillion rubles (€26.9 billion) in cash since February as internet blackouts and economic uncertainty undermine confidence in electronic payments. The surge has left banks short of liquidity, forcing the central bank to inject billions of rubles into the financial system.

Wildberries Warehouses Burn Near St. Petersburg, Flamingo Missile Reportedly Hits Defense Plant — Russian officials reported drone strikes on Wildberries logistics hubs near St. Petersburg, while OSINT analysts said a missile-production plant in Kirov was also hit by Flamingo missile. Wildberries confirmed disruptions, but Ukraine has not officially acknowledged responsibility.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, July 23, 2026 — Latest from the Institute for the Study of War.

Fedorov Turns Down Zelensky’s Deputy PM Offer as Protests Enter Eighth Day — Mykhailo Fedorov rejected President Volodymyr Zelensky’s offer to become deputy prime minister for military innovations, insisting he would only return as defense minister. Protests calling for his reinstatement continued in Kyiv for an eighth consecutive day.

Zelensky to Meet Trump and Attend Lindsey Graham’s Funeral on Upcoming US Trip, Sources Say — President Volodymyr Zelensky is expected to visit the US on Sunday and meet US President Donald Trump, according to diplomatic sources cited by Suspilne. The trip is also expected to include attendance at Senator Lindsey Graham’s funeral.

Russian Attacks on Black Sea Ships Spark Global Food Security Warning — Ukraine and Poland warned that intensified Russian attacks on civilian vessels in the Black Sea risk disrupting global food supplies. The two foreign ministers also discussed new EU sanctions, Ukraine’s membership bid and the need for greater pressure on Moscow.

Russian FIDE Chief Steps Aside After EU Sanctions Over Ukraine — FIDE President Arkady Dvorkovich has suspended his duties after the EU sanctioned him over actions linked to Russia’s occupation of Ukrainian territory. Former world chess champion Viswanathan Anand will serve as interim president.

Rubio Signals Shift in US Ukraine Diplomacy After Talks With Lavrov — US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in Manila, but the talks produced no visible progress toward ending Russia’s war against Ukraine. Rubio said Washington may need new proposals after previous approaches failed to win acceptance from both Kyiv and Moscow.

Russia Approves State-Funded IVF for Widows as Birth Rates Hit Historic Low — Russia’s State Duma has approved state-funded fertility treatment for women whose husbands died fighting in Ukraine. Beginning Dec. 1, eligible widows may receive IVF or artificial insemination for five years after their spouse’s death, provided they do not remarry.

Southern Rumblings, (More) Burning Tanks, Gen-Z Angst and War — Ukraine’s Defense Minister Fedorov resigned after clashing with Gen. Syrsky over strategy. Meanwhile, Ukraine hit Russia hard: sank the FSB ship Izumrud near Novorossiysk, damaged tankers south of Kerch, hit oil refineries, Wildberries warehouses, and 172+ “shadow fleet” vessels since Operation MoLochKa began. This page compiles the top headlines and critical updates from across Ukraine, offering a real-time snapshot of key developments. Russia Strikes Zaporizhzhia with 5 Aerial Bombs, Injuring 25 Including a 3-Month-Old — Russia struck Zaporizhzhia with five guided aerial bombs, hitting residential neighborhoods and a medical facility. The attack injured 25 people, including six children and a three-month-old baby, according to Ukrainian authorities.

Russian Forces Strike Sloviansk with Aerial Bombs, Wound 14, Damage 7 Buildings — A Russian airstrike on a residential neighborhood in Sloviansk, in the Donetsk region, wounded at least 14 people and damaged seven five-story apartment buildings. Three fires covering about 630 square meters (about 6,781 square feet) broke out.

Ukraine Hits 3 Russian Targets, Including Tanker in Black Sea, Pontoon Crossing — Ukrainian forces struck a tanker in the Black Sea, a pontoon crossing near Novoekonomichne and a Russian troop concentration in Horlivka overnight on Thursday, July 23. The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) said the operation targeted military and economic assets supporting Moscow’s war effort.

Ukraine, Raytheon Discuss Joint Patriot Interceptor Production — Ukraine is prepared to jointly produce Patriot interceptors with Raytheon as the sides seek to deepen their defense partnership, President Volodymyr Zelensky said. The proposed cooperation comes after his discussions with US President Donald Trump in Ankara, Turkey during a NATO summit.

3 Killed, 32 Wounded in Russian Attacks on Dnipropetrovsk Region — Three people were killed and 32 wounded, including a child, as Russian forces struck four districts of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region. Nearly 40 attacks with drones, artillery, and aerial bombs damaged homes, businesses, and a fire station.

EU Sanctions Russia's Sports Minister and FIDE President in 21st Package — The EU has added Russian Sports Minister Mikhail Degtyarev and International Chess Federation (FIDE) President Arkady Dvorkovich to its sanctions list under the newly agreed 21st package. The measures also freeze the oil price cap at $44.1 per barrel and target nearly 250 other individuals.

US Influencer Loomer Attacks Putin for Bombing 11th-Century Ukrainian Religious Edifice — Laura Loomer used a visit to Kyiv’s Pechersk Lavra to renounce her former pro-Russian views, saying Kremlin propaganda misled her. Ukrainian media welcomed her reversal as evidence that some influential US right-wing politicos are shifting toward support for Ukraine.

Rubio Says Russia Is Losing Over 5,000 Troops a Week in Ukraine — US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Russia is losing more than 5,000 to 6,000 soldiers each week, while acknowledging that Ukraine also continues to suffer heavy military and civilian losses.

Chinese Refineries Turn to Russian, Iranian Crude Due to Choked Supplies — Private Chinese refiners are reportedly buying crude from Russia’s Far East and resumed talks with Iran for Iranian crude over supply uncertainty due to renewed fighting in the Middle East. Though Kyiv’s drone strikes dealt a heavy blow to Russia’s oil infrastructure, earlier reports suggest that Russia’s overall fossil fuel exports still made a net profit in May.

Fedorov Turns Down Zelensky’s Offer to Become ‘Deputy PM for Military Innovations’ — The former defense minister wrote in a written response that he would accept no other position than his former post, saying it’s the only way for him to fulfill his plans to reform the military and contribute to Ukraine’s victory against Russia’s invasion.

Russia Escalating Bid to Choke Ukraine’s Grain Corridor as Ships Stay Away – Zelensky — President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia is intensifying efforts to choke Ukraine’s Black Sea grain corridor after no commercial ships entered the country’s ports. The disruption has prompted major shipping companies to suspend port calls, threatening Ukraine’s exports and adding fresh pressure to global food markets.

Zelensky Confirms Ambassador Offer for Former PM Svyrydenko — Zelensky confirmed that he offered former PM Svyrydenko the post of Kyiv’s envoy to Washington alongside another unspecified alternative, but it’s unclear whether Svyrydenko took up any of Zelensky’s offer, as reports suggest that she already turned down the ambassador proposal.

$50M Buk-M3 Blown Off the Road: Ukrainian Drone Ambushes Russian Air Defense System — A Ukrainian drone struck a Russian Buk-M3 air defense system worth an estimated $50 million while it was being moved toward the front line in the Donetsk region, with Ukraine’s Border Guard calling the attack another example of low-cost drones destroying some of Russia’s most valuable military assets.

Fedorov Offered ‘Military Innovation Deputy PM’ Post, Zelensky Says — Zelensky said Thursday he offered former defense minister Fedorov the role of “deputy prime minister of Ukraine for military innovations,” but it’s unclear if the latter had accepted the offer. The proposed position would mean an entirely new ministry, which also casts doubt on whether Fedorov would have actual leverage within the system without an established ministry.

To the Ukrainians, Zelensky is Not a Hero, Just a Politician | Stefan Korshak — The dismissal of Ukraine’s popular Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has sparked protests across the country. Many saw his sacking over reported conflict with top commander Oleksandr Syrskyi as a massive blunder by President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Drones vs. Humans- Ukraine's Defense Reshuffle — Drones vs. humans is driving the evolution of warfare worldwide. It is also what is driving Zelensky's firing of both his defense minister and the general of his armies at a crucial time.

Ukrainian F-16 Shoots Down Russian Su-35 in First Aerial Kill, US General Says — The senior US general told the Senate that a Ukrainian F-16 shot down a Russian Su-35 in a recent engagement, marking the first known F-16-versus-Su-35 air combat victory. The Su-35 forms the backbone of Russia’s fighter fleet and has been exported to several countries, including Iran.

Russia's Su-57 Fifth-Generation Fighter Jet Crashes Near Moscow — A Russian Su-57 fifth-generation fighter jet crashed during a training flight near Moscow. The pilot ejected safely, no casualties were reported, and Russian authorities have not yet disclosed the cause of the incident.

Russia Warns US Against Ukraine Arms Sales as Top Diplomats Meet in Manila — Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov told US Secretary of State Marco Rubio that further American arms deliveries to Ukraine were “unacceptable” during talks in Manila, while urging a diplomatic solution. The meeting came as Kyiv seeks to revive peace efforts and Washington shifts focus back to ending the war.

Irish PM Visits Kyiv as Ireland Makes Ukraine Top EU Presidency Priority — Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin arrived in Kyiv for talks with President Volodymyr Zelensky, pledging Ireland will make support for Ukraine and its EU membership bid a top priority during its six-month presidency of the Council of the EU.

EU Agrees on 21st Russia Sanctions Package — EU ambassadors have agreed on the bloc’s 21st sanctions package against Russia after weeks of disputes over measures targeting Moscow. The deal follows objections from several member states that forced Brussels to scale back some proposals, but the package will still expand economic pressure on the Kremlin.

Russia Restricts Nighttime Shipping at its Largest Cargo Port After Ukrainian Drone Attacks — Russia has reportedly imposed nighttime restrictions at Novorossiysk, its largest cargo port, as Ukrainian attacks disrupt Black Sea shipping. The measures, alongside disruptions on Ukraine’s coast, have tightened grain export routes and pushed wheat prices higher.

Kremlin Prepares for Mobilization as Putin Downplays Deepening Fuel Crisis — ISW says Russia is preparing legal and security measures for possible mobilization while bracing for domestic unrest. Despite worsening fuel shortages and mounting economic pressure, Putin insists the economy remains stable and resilient.

223-Drone Raid Hits Russian Regions, Sparking Fires at Oil and Energy Facilities — Ukraine reportedly struck a Wildberries logistics hub, an oil refinery, and a major oil pipeline station during overnight drone attacks. Russia said it intercepted 223 drones while acknowledging casualties and damage across several regions.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, July 22, 2026 — Latest from the Institute for the Study of War.

Wartime Resilience: The ‘Silver Lining’ in Ukraine’s Leadership Shake-Up — The Washington Post highlights the strength of Ukrainian civil society after the leadership shake-up, with Thursday’s military consultations set to test what comes next.

Explosions Rock Occupied Crimea as Drones Reportedly Target Sevastopol and Yalta — The latest reported drone attack on occupied Crimea focused on military and energy-related infrastructure, including positions near Sevastopol and sites in Yalta.

Ukraine Calls Emergency UN Meeting as Russian Strikes Halt Black Sea Shipping — Kyiv has called for an urgent UN Security Council meeting after Russian attacks disrupted civilian shipping and further strained Ukraine’s Black Sea grain exports.

Ukrainian Soldiers Welcome Drapaty as Army Chief but Still Want Fedorov Back — Ukrainian soldiers and civilians welcomed Mykhailo Drapaty’s appointment as army commander, while many continued to call for former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov to return to government.

Rubio, Lavrov to Hold First Face-to-Face Meeting Since September in Manila to Discuss Ukraine — US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov are set for their first in-person meeting since September, with Ukraine at the center of discussions.

Zelensky Invited to Graham Funeral as Kyiv Plans Possible Trump Meeting — Ukraine is considering a late-July visit by President Volodymyr Zelensky to the US for Lindsey Graham’s funeral and a possible meeting with President Donald Trump.

UK Warns OSCE That Russia's Attacks Risk Wider European Escalation — Russia’s aerial campaign against Ukraine has killed at least 20 civilians in one recent overnight strike, the UK told the OSCE, adding that Russia repeatedly violated NATO and Moldovan airspace, increasing the risk of wider escalation.

Zelensky Speaks With Witkoff, Kushner on Advancing Ukraine Peace Talks — President Volodymyr Zelensky spoke with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner about intensifying diplomacy toward ending the Russian war, saying Ukraine has long been ready for peace and thanking US President Donald Trump for continued US support.

Angola Court Jails 2 Russian Spies on Espionage, Terrorism Charges — Angola has jailed two Russians for 11 and 8 years respectively under charges that range from espionage to terrorism. Authorities accused the two of paying locals over $24,000 to spread anti-Western and pro-Russian propaganda and staging deadly protests, but the two denied the charges by arguing they were merely in the country to establish a Russian cultural center.

Czech Ministries Draft Law to Let Companies, Police Down Stray Drones — The Czech Interior and Transport Ministries have drafted legislation allowing police and infrastructure operators to eliminate drones flying illegally near critical sites. The bill, now in interagency review, sets clear no-fly zones with defined intervention rules.

Belarus to Send Poorly Performing Farmers to Guard Ukraine Border — Belarusian leader Alexander Lukashenko said underperforming harvest workers – and officials – should be sent to the army to guard the Ukraine border as Minsk rallied for a bountiful harvest season. Despite the call, he said he has no intention to start a war with Ukraine, framing the order as a way to improve the workers’ general wellbeing.

Russian Strikes Wound 7 in Dnipropetrovsk Region — Russian armed forces attacked two districts of Ukraine’s Dnipropetrovsk region more than 40 times with drones, artillery, and an aerial bomb, wounding seven people and damaging infrastructure and homes.

Russia Expands Prison Recruitment for Ukraine War With New Bill — Russia’s State Duma passed a bill on Wednesday to broaden the pool of potential military recruits from among prisoners, with those serving a sentence for organized crime and mishandling state secrets also eligible for service amid recent reports that Moscow has failed to hit its recruitment targets despite higher financial incentives.

Hungary Blocks EU Clusters 2,3 for Ukraine, Moldova’s Accession Talks — Hungary refused to approve EU accession clusters 2 and 3 for the second time, scheduling the next attempt for Sept. 1. Budapest previously argued that opening all clusters at once wouldn’t be fair to other candidates in the Western Balkans.

Why Is Ukraine Attacking Wildberries? Here’s Why — Ukraine has destroyed several more warehouses belonging to Wildberries, one of Russia’s largest retail businesses. The attacks have dealt a serious blow to Russia’s small and medium-sized businesses. But what lies behind Ukraine’s strikes?

Zelensky Receives Washington’s NATO Envoy in Kyiv to Talk Air Defense, Drone Deal — President Volodymyr Zelensky said he discussed the Patriot’s transfers and licensed production in Kyiv with US Ambassador to NATO Matthew Whitaker and Lt. Gen. Curtis Buzzard, the commander of NATO Security Assistance & Training for Ukraine. Zelensky said the parties also signed an agreement to advance the “Drone Deal,” while other reports suggest that it paves the way for official testing of Ukrainian drones
Russia Moves to ‘Cancel’ Political Exiles With Asset Freezes — Rights lawyers call it the “de facto deprivation of citizenship,” while Moscow pressures them to return and “confess.”

Germany Approves Controversial French-Russian Nuclear Project — Germany has approved a Framatome-Rosatom project in Lingen to produce fuel rods for Russian-designed reactors, despite warnings it could expose sensitive nuclear infrastructure to spying and sabotage risks.

'Gasoline Situation Is F***ed' – Fuel Crisis Hits Russian Army as Troops Report Severe Shortages — Russian soldiers say fuel shortages caused by Ukraine's refinery strikes have led to rationing, disrupted logistics, and higher costs. Some troops report walking miles for supplies as volunteer groups also appeal for gasoline donations.

Ukraine’s New Military Commander Maj. Gen. Mykhailo Drapaty: 5 Things to Know — Mykhailo Drapaty, Ukraine’s new senior officer, is renowned for frontline leadership since 2014. He pioneered large-scale drone-centric warfare, helped liberate Kherson, and is respected for decentralized command, innovation, and accepting responsibility for battlefield failures.

UK, Germany Team Up on Secret Long-Range Missile to Strike Russia — Britain and Germany are developing a classified missile under the Deep Precision Strike program. The project aims to strengthen NATO's long-range strike capability while reducing Europe's reliance on US military systems.

Lavrov, Rubio to Meet in Manila as Kremlin Hardens Ukraine Position — Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov will meet US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Manila for their first face-to-face talks since September, as the Kremlin reportedly abandons the idea of a territorial swap with Ukraine and doubles down on plans to retain occupied border areas as a buffer zone.

Ukraine: Why Was Army Chief Syrskyi Fired? — President Volodymyr Zelensky replaced Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi with General Mykhailo Drapatyi after protests sparked by the dismissal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov. Commentators are divided: some see the move as a response to public pressure and a step toward military reform, while others praise Syrskyi’s wartime record or criticize Zelensky’s leadership style.

‘An Enormous Shitstorm Is Coming’: Russians React to Ukraine’s Wildberries Strikes — “Many people will wake up bankrupt,” one Russian seller said after another Wildberries warehouse went up in flames. A series of Ukrainian drone strikes has exposed fear, anger, and doubts about the Kremlin’s ability to protect Russia’s logistics network.

Ukraine's Drone Offensive Hits 13 Russian Ships and Crimea's Power Grid in 48 Hours — Ukraine says its drones struck 13 Russian vessels and 13 energy facilities over two days. The attacks are part of separate campaigns targeting Russia's maritime logistics and power infrastructure in occupied Crimea and other occupied territories.

Zelensky Appoints Major General Ihor Skybiuk as New Chief of Ukraine’s General Staff Amid Military Shake-Up — Volodymyr Zelensky has appointed Major General Ihor Skybiuk as the new Chief of Ukraine’s General Staff, completing a major military leadership reshuffle that also saw Mykhailo Drapaty named the new AFU commander-in-chief.

Kremlin Rules Out Returning Occupied Sumy, Kharkiv Border Areas in Peace Deal – Bloomberg — Russia no longer plans to return occupied parts of Ukraine’s Sumy and Kharkiv regions in any future peace deal, according to Bloomberg. The Kremlin reportedly intends to keep the border areas as buffer zones while pressing ahead with its goal of capturing the entire Donetsk and Luhansk regions.

Lithuania Moves Red Army Graves to Leave Behind Soviet Past — Lithuania is exhuming Soviet Red Army graves as part of its drive to erase symbols of Soviet occupation, drawing sharp protests from Moscow. The wartime memorial relocations have become the latest flashpoint in a broader battle over history, memory, and Russia’s influence in the Baltic region.

EU’s New Russia Sanctions Stall as Member States Defend Own Interests — The EU is pushing to approve its 21st Russia sanctions package, but internal disputes over LNG, shipping, banking and trade have forced major compromises. Despite Viktor Orbán’s departure from Hungary’s leadership, member states are still struggling to agree on how far to go in pressuring Moscow.

Putin’s AI Army: Deepfakes Posing as Polish Soldiers Spread Kremlin Lies About Ukraine — Polish authorities say Kremlin-linked actors used AI-generated videos posing as Polish soldiers to spread anti-Ukrainian narratives. Cybersecurity experts identified Russian-language traces and other manipulation, while several accounts were later removed.

Syrsky Says Army Went From Defense to Offensive Before Exit as Russia Declares Drapatyi Wanted — Outgoing AFU chief Syrsky defended his wartime leadership, highlighting battlefield gains and military reforms. Meanwhile, Russia placed newly appointed Commander-in-Chief Drapatyi on its wanted list without specifying the charges.

Ukraine Strikes 2 Major Logistics Hubs of Russia’s Largest Online Retailer — Ukrainian drones struck two of Wildberries' largest logistics centers in southern Russia, injuring several people and hitting an oil depot. The attack follows previous strikes on the retailer's distribution network.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, July 21, 2026 — Latest from the Institute for the Study of War.

Syrsky Out, Drapaty In: Fedorov Welcomes Shakeup as Zelensky Offers Him ‘Worthy Position’ — President Volodymyr Zelensky has replaced Gen. Oleksandr Syrsky with Maj. Gen. Mykhailo Drapaty as Ukraine’s new commander-in-chief following six days of nationwide protests over Mykhailo Fedorov’s dismissal. Fedorov welcomed the move as “a breath of fresh air and new hope,” while Zelensky offered him a new technology-focused government role.

Inside Dnipro Hospital Where Russian Drone Wounds Have Replaced Bullet Injuries — Dnipro’s central hospital has become a key treatment center for soldiers and civilians wounded across eastern and southern Ukraine. Doctors say the nature of injuries has changed since Russia’s full-scale invasion, with bullet wounds increasingly replaced by devastating trauma from drones, missiles and glide bombs.

US Senate Places Ukraine Aid Bill on Calendar — The US Senate has completed the Rule 14 process for H.R. 2913, the Ukraine Support Act, placing the House-passed bill directly on the Senate Calendar of Business. The procedural move bypasses traditional committee review and allows Senate leadership to bring the measure to the floor, though it does not guarantee a vote. The bill includes military support, reconstruction aid and expanded Russia sanctions.

UN Says Civilian Casualties in Ukraine War Rose 37 Percent in First Half of 2026 — Civilian casualties in Russia’s war against Ukraine rose by 37 percent in the first half of 2026, AFP reported, citing the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine. Danielle Bell said monitors documented 1,396 civilians killed and 7,978 injured, with long-range ballistic missiles, drones, glide bombs and FPV drones driving the increase.

Azerbaijan Confirms Secret German-Russian Talks Were Held in Baku — Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev confirmed that former German and Russian officials held secret talks in Baku earlier this month to discuss possible ways to end Russia’s war against Ukraine. Speaking alongside German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Berlin, Aliyev said Azerbaijan was not officially informed by either side.
